text:
emma: Heading into the publish window for py/ts SDKs. Canaries queued, but I want a quick seatbelt check before we flip traffic. :seatbelt:
deploy-bot: Canaries started: py-canary-2026-03-21 (replicas 2), ts-canary-2026-03-21 (replicas 2). Link: https://ci/internal/build/6721 :rocket:
raj: Thanks — what's the rollback signal here? If we see >0.5% error spike on lib usage or signer mismatch on wheels, we pull canary and pin previous disttag? :thinking_face:
marta: +1 on signer mismatch. Also watch checksum diff for wheels/tar.gz vs artifact registry. If checksum != expected, we immediately yank and retag with beta-disttag.
ken: Quick checklist: 1) publish artifacts to staging registry 2) smoke install `pip install redwood-sdk==canary` and `npm i @redwood/sdk@canary` 3) run basic smoke tests 4) check telemetry for token usage regression.
paul: I'm on smoke installs now. Py canary installs clean, TS has a TypeScript typedef break in the generated types for `ClientOptions.timeout`. Investigating. :eyes:
emma: If TS typedef break is real, we should hold the final cut and publish a patch. No hotfixes during the window unless it's a release-blocker. Let's decide by +15m.
sre-oncall: FYI load on dedicated CI infra is spiking; if we see flaky integ tests, treat as infra flakiness and re-run once before rollback. Incident link: https://infra/inc/8892
raj: For rollback mechanics: we pin `latest` to the previous published tag (e.g., `2026-03-19-stable`) and push a disttag `canary-hold` for troubleshooting tenants. Also update release notes draft to mark the TS typedef as gated if we hold.
paul: TS break is in a generator script diff. Can probably patch and republish canary within 20m. I prefer republish vs rollback.
emma: Agreed — republish canary after patch. If new canary passes installs + telemetry sanity in 10m, we proceed to GA cut.
deploy-bot: py-canary-2026-03-21: smoke passed. ts-canary-2026-03-21: smoke failed (typedef error).
marta: OK let's stop the GA cut. @paul can you publish a patched canary and ping here when uploaded? Also tag the release notes with "hold: TS typedef" and add a short snippet for customers who pinned types.
paul: Patch pushed, new canary published: ts-canary-2026-03-21-rc2. Artifact URL: registry.corp/npm/@redwood/sdk/ts-canary-rc2
ken: Re-running smoke installs and sample app tests now.
paul: smoke installs clean. Basic runtime test on sample-app passes.
raj: Telemetry: no abnormal token errors in the last 5m post-republish. We should be safe to proceed with GA cut in 5m.
emma: I'll coordinate the cut. Reminder: update release notes with migration guide for `ClientOptions.timeout` change and add a compatibility note for pinned type consumers. Also call out pinning strategy for customers: prefer `dist-tag: stable` or explicit version ranges.
sre-oncall: No infra alerts. Proceeding.
deploy-bot: Starting GA publish job: publish-py-2026-03-21, publish-ts-2026-03-21. Logs: https://ci/internal/publish/9812 :shipit:
paul: One more ask — add a short note in release notes about checksum verification steps we used for this window (so customers can verify artifacts).
emma: Done. Release notes updated: https://docs.internal/releases/2026-03-21-sdk-release (draft).
rab: (typo) — whoops ignore last message.
raj: After GA, let's create a short postmortem doc for the typedef slip and add a small test to generator to catch it. Assigning to @paul and @marta.
emma: Thanks everyone. Moving to postpublish monitoring: watch for error spikes for 30m and open rollback if >1% error increase or any checksum/signature alerts.
deploy-bot: Publish jobs finished: success. Artifacts pinned: py@2026-03-21, ts@2026-03-21.
paul: I'll follow up with the generator test and PR.
marta: I'll finalize the release notes and ship the announcement in #announcements at 16:30 UTC. :tada:
emma: Closing thread — will reopen if any rollback criteria hit. Thanks all.
